prompt.en: Explain why a growing cell eventually divides into two smaller cells instead of simply continuing to grow larger and larger.

label.en: Larger cells struggle to transport materials

level1.en: As a cell gets bigger, what happens to the distance materials must travel inside it?

clue.en: Nutrients, proteins and waste all have farther to travel to reach every part of a much bigger cell.

level2Template.en: As a cell grows larger, materials must travel longer ___ to reach all parts of the cell.

label.en: One copy of DNA struggles to coordinate a much bigger cell

level1.en: Every activity in the cell depends on its DNA. What happens to that single copy of instructions as the cell gets bigger?

clue.en: The same one set of instructions now has to coordinate far more organelles, proteins and chemical reactions than before.

level2Template.en: As the cell becomes larger, its single copy of ___ must coordinate an increasingly complex, overloaded cell.

label.en: Dividing produces smaller, more manageable daughter cells

level1.en: Instead of continuing to grow, what alternative strategy does the cell use to solve this problem?

clue.en: Rather than growing into one enormous cell, it splits into two, each of which is easier to run and can keep growing on its own.

level2Template.en: Instead of growing indefinitely, a cell can ___ into two smaller, more manageable cells.

text.en: A larger cell contains more material to manage, and eventually being larger becomes a disadvantage instead of an advantage.
Materials must travel longer ___ to reach every part of a bigger cell.
The cell's one copy of ___ must now coordinate more organelles, proteins and reactions than before.
Instead of growing forever, the cell can ___ into two smaller cells that are each easier to manage.
